messages:
Ara: Quick Q — seeing AccessDenied when decrypting a wrapped data key in eu-west-1 using a replica MRK from account 2222 during a regional failover test. Anyone hit this?
Ara: CLI call: `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://dk.enc --region eu-west-1` -> `AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::2222:assumed-role/failover-role is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:3333:key/replica-uuid`
Jamal: Did you add the cross-account principal into the replica key policy? For MRKs you need explicit allowance on the replica (or a grant). Also confirm the role has kms:Decrypt in its IAM policy — both sides matter.
Sophia: Small note — MRKs are special: if it's a true multi-region key (primary + replica relationship), replicas can decrypt ciphertext produced by the primary _if_ the replication relationship exists and policy allows it. If someone just created an independent key with the same alias, it won't work.
kms-bot: replica kms key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:3333:key/replica-uuid created (replica-of arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:3333:key/primary-uuid)
Oliver: Also check which endpoint you're hitting. If the call targets the wrong region or the wrong key ARN, you can get policy mismatch. For cross-account decrypts the simplest reliable pattern we've used is: primary creates a grant for the cross-account role, and a matching policy on the replica allows that principal.
Ara: here's the replica key policy I tried (still failing):
```json
{
  "Version":"2012-10-17",
  "Id":"key-default-1",
  "Statement":[
    {
      "Sid":"AllowAccountBDecrypt",
      "Effect":"Allow",
      "Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::2222:role/failover-role"},
      "Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:DescribeKey"],
      "Resource":"*"
    }
  ]
}
```
Jamal: That looks generally OK but confirm it's applied to the replica key resource in eu-west-1 (not only on the primary). Also check for `kms:ViaService` or condition keys that might be implicitly blocking. CloudTrail will tell you which keyId was used.
Sophia: Quick test to isolate: from account B (failover role) run:
```bash
# encrypt under primary (us-east-1)
aws kms encrypt --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:3333:key/primary-uuid --plaintext 'test' --output text --query CiphertextBlob | base64 -d > /tmp/test.enc
# try decrypt in replica region (eu-west-1)
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb:///tmp/test.enc --region eu-west-1
```
If that fails it's definitely a policy/grant issue. If it succeeds then the problem is how your data key was generated or wrapped in the app path.
Ara: ran that exact flow. It fails with the same AccessDenied. CloudTrail shows a Decrypt event error on keyId arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:3333:key/replica-uuid.
Oliver: Two pragmatic fixes: (1) add the failover-role principal to the replica key policy in eu-west-1, or (2) create a revocable Grant from the primary account/key to the failover-role (grants are good for automated failover because they are easy to revoke). Our infra team prefers grants for ephemeral access.
Sophia: On rotation: rotating the CMK (automatic KMS rotation or replacing the primary) doesn't invalidate existing ciphertext — KMS manages key versions. But if you rewrap data keys or re-encrypt blobs you must run a rewrap/ReEncrypt job. For large stores prefer envelope encryption and an offline rewrap pipeline using `ReEncrypt` so you don't have to decrypt plaintext in your app.
Jamal: CloudTrail debug tips: filter for `eventSource: kms.amazonaws.com` and `eventName: Decrypt`. Check `requestParameters.keyId`, `responseElements.errorMessage`, and `userIdentity` fields to see exactly which principal was denied and which key ARN was targeted. That points to key policy vs IAM mismatch.
Ara: Plan: 1) add explicit principal to replica key policy for arn:aws:iam::2222:role/failover-role in eu-west-1; 2) have primary create a short-lived grant to the role during the sync job; 3) add `aws kms list-grants --key-id arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:3333:key/replica-uuid` and `aws kms list-key-policies --key-id <replica>` into the failover checklist; 4) add a smoke test that encrypts in primary and decrypts in replica.
kms-bot: created grant 1234abcd to arn:aws:iam::2222:role/failover-role (expires in 7d)
Oliver: Also be mindful of org SCPs / condition keys or KMS endpoint VPC restrictions — those can silently block even when policies look correct. Test from the exact runtime environment used in failover.
Ara: can someone add the runbook steps to infra-runbooks and a CI smoke test? I’ll follow up with a PR for the policy snippet.
Sophia: I'll open the PR with a minimal example policy + test harness. Minimal policy snippet for cross-account decrypt (to include in the PR):
```json
{
  "Version":"2012-10-17",
  "Statement":[
    {
      "Effect":"Allow",
      "Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::2222:role/failover-role"},
      "Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:DescribeKey"],
      "Resource":"*"
    }
  ]
}
```
Ara: great — marking this thread as actionable. I'll update when PR/Smoke tests land and after next DR drill. Thanks all!
